mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP and housing conditions reverse within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the unemployment rate reverts below 5% within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output and input demand, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in industrial production reverses within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which raises real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo moving avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo moving avg
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 400k per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or payroll growth decelerates sharply within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a robust recovery in aggregate demand, which lifts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or either proxy reverts below baseline within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a sustained expansion in supply capacity, which supports higher corporate revenues and profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or INDPRO growth falls below 0.2% MoM within the horizon.
